Lease-based shard claiming for cooperative crawlers

A. Researcher, B. Coauthor

Keywords: crawlers, leases, work stealing

Abstract

We describe a shard queue that hands out time-bounded leases instead of fixed partitions. The design removes the hot counter that limits naive work stealing, and it recovers from worker failure without a central coordinator.

1. Introduction

Partitioned crawlers assign each worker a fixed range of uniform resource locators before the run starts. When one host is slower than the rest, the range becomes a straggler and the whole run waits for it[1].

2. Method

A worker claims a shard by writing an expiring lease into the queue, then renews the lease while it makes progress. A dead worker stops renewing, and the shard returns to the queue after the lease expires.

3. Results

Across 40 runs the queue depth never exceeded twice the pool size, and the tail of the run was 31 percent shorter than a fixed partition of the same shards[2].

References

  1. R. Author. Partitioned fetch scheduling. Journal of Example Systems, 2024.
